# 0069: Decisions endpoint rates do not price agent runs

Status: accepted, 2026-10-13.
Extends [0051](0051-long-context-is-a-tier-priced-per-call-and-records-are-curated.md) with a deliberate exclusion for another endpoint's token rates.

## Context

LiteLLM now carries Decisions endpoint rates beside Responses rates on `gpt-6-luna`.
Those `_decisions` fields make the curator stop at its unknown-cost-field check.
OpenAI's [Decisions documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions) limits those rates to `/v1/decisions`.
Codex uses Responses, so applying Decisions rates would price its runs incorrectly.

## Decision

**Recognised Decisions token-rate fields are deliberately excluded.** A field must match an existing base or long-context token-rate name plus `_decisions`.
An arbitrary cost field ending in `_decisions` remains unknown and stops the write.
`derive/feed.py` applies this rule to both bundled curation and live pricing.

**Responses rates and thresholds remain authoritative for agent runs.** Decisions rates never replace base rates or the long-context tier.
A regression test covers the feed's base and long-context Decisions fields together, alongside an unknown Decisions cost field.

## Consequences

Curation can refresh the catalogue from the current feed without adopting another endpoint's pricing.
The unknown-cost-field boundary remains closed for unrecognised pricing dimensions.
Historical rates stay reproducible in dated records, and a refresh closes the open interval without editing its rates.

## Lens

A model id alone does not establish which endpoint's rates apply.
Exclude another endpoint's recognised fields explicitly, and keep refusing pricing dimensions nobody has reviewed.
